days.recap: Discover and assess workloads first, then pick retain, retire, rehost, replatform, refactor or reimagine for each. Compare VMs, containers and serverless by how much operations Google takes over, use Spot VMs only for interruptible work, and rely on Kubernetes, autoscaling and load balancing for scale and availability.

days.title: Google Cloud Compute Choices and Hybrid Products

concepts.heading: Compute Engine for Control and Least Change
concepts.body: Compute Engine is Google Cloud's infrastructure as a service for virtual machines. The customer picks the machine configuration and operating system, installs its own software and administers the VM, while Google runs the physical data centers, hardware and network. Its business value is least change and speed: software that expects a specific operating system, an agent or full machine access can move as it is, and VMs appear in minutes instead of waiting for hardware orders. Machine types are flexible: predefined types for general, compute-heavy and memory-heavy needs, custom machine types, and types with GPU or TPU accelerators for AI. A risk team whose workloads differ in shape can therefore right-size each one. Remember the limit: this is IaaS, so Google does not patch the guest operating system or the applications inside the VM, and VMs do not turn themselves into containers. A manufacturer whose vendor package needs a particular OS and cannot be rewritten should choose Compute Engine.

concepts.heading: Google Kubernetes Engine
concepts.body: Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) is a managed Kubernetes service: Google operates the control plane and can manage the nodes, while the customer runs containerized applications. It suits a company with dozens of containerized services that wants Kubernetes features such as rolling updates, automatic scaling and self-healing without operating Kubernetes itself. GKE has two modes of operation that differ in how much control the customer keeps. In Standard mode, experienced engineers tune node hardware, networking and scheduling themselves, which gives control with more responsibility. In Autopilot mode, Google manages the nodes, which reduces operational work for teams that want to focus on their applications. A platform team full of Kubernetes experts who must tune node configuration prefers Standard, while a small team that wants Kubernetes without managing nodes prefers Autopilot. Choosing GKE signals that the organization has standardized on containers and wants orchestration, portability and microservices, not that it wants the least operations possible, for which serverless is stronger.

concepts.heading: Cloud Run and Cloud Run Functions
concepts.body: Cloud Run is a serverless platform that runs containers. Developers hand over a container and the platform scales it with incoming requests, including down to zero when nobody is calling, and charges for use. That fits unpredictable traffic: a media company's web app that spikes during live events and drops to nothing afterwards pays little in the quiet hours and needs no capacity planning. Cloud Run functions runs small pieces of code in response to events, and the team pays only while the code executes. An online photo service that wants thumbnails created each time a customer uploads a picture is the textbook case: the upload is the event, and the function is the response. The difference to remember is the unit of deployment. A container service such as Cloud Run suits a whole web application or API; a function suits a single short reaction to an event. Both hide the server and the operating system, so neither fits a vendor package that needs its own OS, which points back to Compute Engine.

concepts.heading: Modern Application Development
concepts.body: Choosing compute is part of a wider shift to modern application development. Organizations move from large monolithic applications, released rarely and scaled all at once, to microservices that are released and scaled independently, packaged as containers, run on managed platforms, and connected through APIs. The business benefits are speed of change, fault isolation and cost that follows use. Managed services support this because Google runs the underlying operations such as patching, backups and scaling, so a startup with three developers can launch in weeks without building database operations. A useful mapping for an exam scenario with three workloads: a legacy package needing its own operating system goes to Compute Engine, a set of containerized microservices needing orchestration goes to GKE, and an unpredictable web service or event reaction goes to Cloud Run or Cloud Run functions. Elastic platforms matter commercially as well, because a retailer that once bought servers for a yearly sale can scale out for the peak and back, so cost follows actual use.

concepts.heading: Hybrid and Multicloud Products
concepts.body: Many organizations cannot or will not move everything to one place. Regulation may require data to stay in a private data center, and acquisitions or customer demand may leave data in other clouds. Google Cloud therefore offers products that bring its capabilities to where the data is. AlloyDB Omni is a downloadable, PostgreSQL-compatible database with Google's enhancements that runs in private data centers, other clouds or elsewhere, which fits a regulated utility that must keep its database on site. BigQuery Omni runs BigQuery analytics on data stored in Amazon S3 or Azure Blob Storage, so a consultancy's BigQuery-trained analysts can query it without first copying it. GKE Enterprise and GKE fleet management group Kubernetes clusters on Google Cloud, on-premises and in other clouds so one group of administrators manages them together. Looker is a business intelligence platform that queries Google Cloud and many other sources in place. The pattern is to bring the familiar tool to the data, instead of forcing the data to move.

examPoints: Needs OS control and cannot be rewritten means Compute Engine; containers needing orchestration means GKE; bursty containers or event reactions mean Cloud Run or Cloud Run functions.
GKE Standard mode gives engineers control of nodes, and Autopilot mode lets Google manage the nodes.
AlloyDB Omni, BigQuery Omni and GKE fleet management bring database, analytics and cluster management to on-premises and other clouds without moving the data.

quiz.q: A software firm's engineers have packaged a stateless web API as a container. Demand is unpredictable and sometimes zero for days. The firm wants no server management and charges only for use. Which service fits best?
choices: Compute Engine, because VMs are billed only while customers send requests to them
Cloud Run, because it runs containers serverlessly and can scale down to zero when idle
GKE Standard mode, because Google then manages the nodes and removes all capacity planning
Cloud Run functions, because every complete web API must be rewritten as a single function
quiz.explain: Cloud Run runs containers without server management and scales with requests, including to zero. Choice C is tempting because GKE is a managed service, but in Standard mode the customer still tunes nodes and plans capacity, so it does not match the goal.

quiz.q: A grocery group has Kubernetes clusters in two of its own data centers and in a second public cloud. A small team wants to manage all of them together from Google Cloud. What helps most?
choices: Cloud Run, because it replaces clusters by running every service on Google's serverless platform
Cloud Run functions, because each cluster could be rewritten as a set of small event handlers
Spot VMs, because reclaimable capacity lets the team shift clusters between providers cheaply
GKE fleet management, because it groups clusters across Google Cloud, on-premises and other clouds
quiz.explain: Fleet management groups clusters wherever they run so they are managed together. Choice A is tempting because serverless reduces operations, but it would mean re-platforming every service, not managing the existing clusters from one place.

days.recap: Compute Engine gives VMs with OS control, GKE gives managed Kubernetes in Standard or Autopilot mode, Cloud Run runs containers serverlessly and Cloud Run functions react to events. AlloyDB Omni, BigQuery Omni and GKE fleet management take Google capabilities to on-premises and other clouds.

days.title: APIs, Apigee, and Domain 4 Consolidation

concepts.heading: What an API Is and Why Executives Care
concepts.body: An application programming interface (API) is a defined way for one software system to request data or actions from another. The provider publishes what can be requested, such as get the balance for this account, and what comes back; the caller does not need to know how the backend works. A bank's mobile app, partner portal and a fintech partner's service can all reach the same account data through one API. Executives care for four reasons. Reuse: one backend capability serves many apps and partners. Speed: developers build on existing APIs instead of rebuilding functions. Decoupling: the backend can change, even be replaced, as long as the API contract holds, which makes gradual modernization possible. Control: the owner decides who may call the API and how often. Do not confuse an API with an SLA, which is a contractual promise about service levels, or with a data lake, which stores raw data. An API is the interface through which applications talk.

concepts.heading: Exposing and Monetizing APIs
concepts.body: Exposing capabilities or data through public-facing APIs lets other developers and companies build on what an organization already owns, turning internal assets into digital products. A national weather service with years of forecast data that only its own website uses could publish it as APIs so travel apps, farming tools and insurers embed the forecasts. The opportunities are new products and ecosystems, wider reach through partners, new revenue and faster innovation because outside developers try ideas the owner would not have built. Revenue can come from usage tiers or packages. A logistics firm that wants to offer different packages of its shipment-tracking APIs to partner developers needs a way to define those packages and bill for them. Mailing copies of data, publishing it only on a website, or giving partners a one-time copy all fail, because the data goes stale, partners cannot build on it, and the owner loses control and visibility of usage. The organization still has to secure, measure and manage what it exposes.

concepts.heading: Apigee API Management
concepts.body: Apigee is Google Cloud's API management platform. It places a proxy layer between backend services and the clients that call them, and on that layer the organization applies policies for security, traffic management, rate limiting and quotas, and gathers analytics on who uses each API and how heavily. A developer portal helps partners discover and use the APIs. It supports several API styles including REST, gRPC, SOAP and GraphQL, and can front services running anywhere. Consider a telecom that exposes many APIs from different backend systems, where each team secures them differently and nobody knows who calls them. Apigee gives one management layer with consistent security, limits and analytics. For monetization, Apigee supports API products and rate plans, which let a firm configure billing, payment models or revenue sharing for API usage. The proxy also protects callers during modernization: an insurer can replace its core system over several years while dozens of apps keep calling a stable API proxy. Apigee manages APIs; it does not host the backend application or store data for analysis.

concepts.heading: Domain 4 Consolidation: Choosing the Compute Option
concepts.body: Pull the domain together with a decision path you can run in your head. First ask what the move is trying to achieve: leave a data center quickly means rehost; fix a painful monolith means refactor; unused system means retire; locked by regulation means retain. Then ask who must control what. Need the operating system or a vendor package that cannot change: Compute Engine. Containerized services needing orchestration, rolling updates and portability: GKE, with Standard mode for control or Autopilot to let Google manage nodes. Whole stateless app or API with bursty traffic: Cloud Run. A single short reaction to an event: Cloud Run functions. The more Google operates, the less control you keep, so match control to a genuine need and avoid choosing a heavier platform out of habit. A retailer with three workloads might put the legacy package on Compute Engine, its microservices on GKE and its promotional site on Cloud Run.

concepts.heading: Domain 4 Consolidation: Hybrid, Managed Services, and Common Traps
concepts.body: Several traps recur in this domain. A lift and shift moves quickly but does not by itself deliver agility or lower cost, since gains come when workloads later use autoscaling or managed services. Managed services such as Cloud SQL, which automates backups, patching and failover for MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server databases, relieve small teams of routine upkeep, and moving a self-managed database to one is replatforming. Spot VMs reduce cost only for interruption-tolerant work. Hybrid and multicloud needs do not always mean moving data: BigQuery Omni analyzes data in Amazon S3 or Azure Blob Storage, AlloyDB Omni runs where regulation requires, and GKE fleet management groups clusters in many places. Apigee is the answer for API security, quotas, analytics and monetization, not for hosting applications or orchestrating containers. When two choices both seem plausible, find the phrase that decides: no rewrite, own operating system, event, container, spike to zero, regulated location, or partner-facing API.

examPoints: An API is a defined way for software to request data or actions from other software, giving reuse, speed, decoupling and control.
Apigee puts a proxy layer in front of backends for consistent security, rate limits, quotas, analytics, a developer portal and, with API products and rate plans, monetization.

Pick compute by the deciding phrase: own OS or no rewrite is Compute Engine, orchestrated containers is GKE, stateless containers that scale to zero is Cloud Run, an event reaction is Cloud Run functions.

quiz.q: A freight company has a valuable route-optimization capability used only by its own dispatchers. Leadership wants outside software firms to build products on it, with usage packages that generate revenue. What combination is most appropriate?
choices: Email a monthly spreadsheet export to interested partner firms and charge them for the file
Publish the capability as APIs, manage them with Apigee, and define API products with rate plans
Move the optimization engine to Spot VMs so partners can reach the dispatchers' servers
Give each partner a full copy of the underlying data so that they can host it themselves
quiz.explain: Public APIs let partners build on the capability, and Apigee API products with rate plans handle packaging and billing. Choice D is tempting because partners would have the data, but copies go stale and the freight company loses control and visibility of usage.

quiz.q: A company has three workloads: a vendor-supplied package that needs a specific operating system, a set of twenty containerized microservices needing rolling updates, and a promotional site that gets traffic only during campaigns. Which placement is best?
choices: The package on Cloud Run, the microservices on Compute Engine, the promotional site on GKE
All three on Cloud Run functions, because serverless is always the lowest-cost choice available
The package on GKE Autopilot, the microservices on Compute Engine, the promotional site on Apigee
The package on Compute Engine, the microservices on GKE, the promotional site on Cloud Run
quiz.explain: OS control points to Compute Engine, orchestrated containers to GKE, and bursty traffic with scale to zero to Cloud Run. Choice B is tempting because serverless is efficient, but functions hide the operating system the package needs and are not a home for a whole microservice set.

days.recap: APIs let software request data or actions, and exposing them turns assets into products. Apigee adds security, quotas, analytics, a developer portal and monetization, and stable API proxies allow gradual modernization. For compute, match the deciding phrase to Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud Run or Cloud Run functions.

days.title: Security Threats, Shared Responsibility, and Core Security Terms

concepts.heading: Common Threats and Their Business Impact
concepts.body: Security questions usually start from a symptom, and your job is to name the threat. A DDoS attack floods a service with traffic from many sources so real customers cannot reach it; it harms availability, not confidentiality. Ransomware locks a company's data and demands payment, and the business impact is halted operations and possible data exposure unless recovery was planned in advance. Phishing is a deceptive message that tricks a person into giving up information or access, while malware is harmful software such as viruses and ransomware. Cryptomining is the unauthorized use of someone's compute to mine currency, and its tell-tale sign is an unexpectedly large bill for busy virtual machines. A third-party risk appears when a partner with trusted access but weak security is breached and the attacker walks through that door. Prompt injection targets large language models: crafted input tells the model to ignore its instructions and leak data. A retailer whose ticket site went dark during a sale was hit by DDoS; a start-up with a huge bill and idle projects was probably cryptomined.

concepts.heading: Misconfiguration, Physical Risk, and Cloud Versus On-Premises
concepts.body: Not every incident is an attack from outside. Misconfiguration, such as a storage bucket left open to the internet or a default password never changed, is a customer-side error and is named in cloud security guidance as a leading cause of cloud data breaches. Physical risk, such as fire or flood at a single data center, is reduced with geographic redundancy: separate zones or regions and backups. When a board member says an on-premises data center feels safer than any cloud, the fair answer is that neither is inherently more or less secure. The difference is who owns which layer. On premises, the company is responsible for the physical facility and the whole stack. In the cloud, the provider takes on the facilities and lower layers, and leading providers build layered, secure-by-design protection into the platform. The company still owns its data, its identities and its configuration choices, so cloud moves work around rather than removing the need for good practice.

concepts.heading: Shared Responsibility and Shared Fate
concepts.body: The shared responsibility model divides security duties between the provider and the customer, and the split moves with the service type. With virtual machines (IaaS) the customer secures the operating system, the database software and the data. With a fully managed software service (SaaS) the provider carries most of the stack. The rule of thumb is that the more managed the service, the more the provider secures, but the customer always owns its data and who can access it. Shared fate is a Google Cloud idea that builds on shared responsibility: rather than only drawing a line and leaving customers on their side of it, Google actively helps customers succeed through secure blueprints, guidance and tools. For an exam answer, remember the sentence shared fate equals shared responsibility plus active help. A bank that moves a database to VMs and its email to SaaS should expect to patch and configure the database but not the email platform.

concepts.heading: The CIA Triad and Control Versus Compliance
concepts.body: The CIA triad is the standard way to describe what security protects. Confidentiality means only authorized people see the data. Integrity means data stays accurate and is not altered by unauthorized changes; an insurer whose script silently changed policy amounts for weeks suffered an integrity failure even though nothing leaked. Availability means systems and data are there when needed, which is what a DDoS attack harms. Two further terms are easily mixed up. Control is your own decisions over who can reach systems and where data is stored. Compliance is meeting, and being able to prove, external laws and standards. A hospital can have strong control and still need compliance evidence for auditors. Cyber resilience goes beyond prevention: it combines preparation, detection, response and recovery so the business can keep serving customers even after an attack succeeds. Security by default means protections are built in from the start, and security posture is the overall state of an organization's security.

concepts.heading: Encryption States, Identity, Zero Trust, and Threat Terms
concepts.body: Data can be protected in three states. Data at rest is stored, data in transit is moving across a network, and data in use is being processed in memory, where it is normally decrypted. Confidential Computing is the Google Cloud offering that keeps data encrypted in use. Sensitive Data Protection discovers, classifies and can mask or de-identify sensitive data such as Social Security numbers so it does not leak. For people, authentication proves who you are, authorization decides what you may do, and auditing records what you did. Least privilege means granting only the permissions a job needs and reviewing them, with extra protection such as multi-factor authentication and monitoring for powerful privileged accounts. Zero trust means no request is trusted just because it comes from inside the network; each is verified using identity and context. Finally, threat intelligence is evidence-based knowledge about attackers and their methods that helps anticipate threats, while threat response is the action taken to contain, investigate and recover.

examPoints: A stem that describes a symptom is testing whether you can name the threat: unreachable site under heavy traffic is DDoS, an unexpected bill for busy machines is cryptomining, and an open bucket is customer-side misconfiguration.

The exam expects you to place a control on the right side of the shared responsibility model: the more managed the service, the more the provider secures, while the customer always keeps its data and access decisions.
Know the matching pairs: confidentiality, integrity and availability; at rest, in transit and in use; authentication, authorization and auditing; control versus compliance.

quiz.q: A clinic's patient portal works normally, but a review shows that one staff member's password was reused on a site that was breached, and attackers then signed in to the portal. Which first improvement best reduces the chance of this happening again?
choices: Moving the portal to a larger virtual machine, so that it can handle sign-in requests from more users at once
Requiring multi-factor authentication for staff, so a stolen password alone is no longer enough to sign in
Encrypting the portal's stored files with a stronger algorithm, so that stolen passwords cannot be read
Adding a second region for the portal, so that attackers cannot reach the original deployment
quiz.explain: Multi-factor authentication strengthens authentication, so a leaked password by itself no longer proves who the user is. Larger machines or a second region help capacity and availability, and stronger file encryption protects data at rest, but none of them stops a valid-looking sign-in.

quiz.q: A retailer runs its web store on virtual machines in Google Cloud. A consultant says that because the store is in the cloud, Google handles all of its security. Which response is correct?
choices: Correct, because the provider secures the operating system and applications on virtual machines as well
Incorrect, because the customer secures only physical access, which the provider cannot manage
Correct, because shared fate means the provider takes over every duty the customer used to hold
Incorrect, because the customer still secures the operating system, applications and data, while Google secures the underlying facilities
quiz.explain: With virtual machines the provider secures the facilities and lower layers, while the customer is responsible for the operating system, software, data and access. Shared fate means Google actively helps customers with blueprints and guidance, not that it takes over the customer's duties.

days.recap: Name the threat from its symptom, place each duty on the correct side of shared responsibility, and remember that Google's shared fate adds active help. Pair the key terms: CIA, at rest, in transit and in use, authentication, authorization and auditing, least privilege, zero trust, and control versus compliance.

days.title: Defense in Depth, Google Cloud Security Products, and Trust

concepts.heading: Secure by Design and Defense in Depth
concepts.body: Google describes its protection with two ideas that appear often in business questions. Secure by design means security is built into Google's own data centers, servers, network equipment and custom security chips, so customers inherit protection from the layers beneath their workloads. A hospital group worried that a cloud provider cannot match its own protection can be told that it is not buying a bare server; it is building on infrastructure whose lower layers Google designed with security in mind. Defense in depth means stacking independent layers of control across facilities, hardware, software, network and data, so that if one control fails the others still limit what an attacker can reach. It is the opposite of relying on one strong perimeter. For the AI era the same layered thinking applies to the AI stack: infrastructure, data, models, platform and agents each need their own protection, which is why Google Cloud offers different tools at different layers.

concepts.heading: Threat Intelligence, Security Command Center, and Security Operations
concepts.body: Three products are easy to blur, so learn what each answers. Google Threat Intelligence tells a security team who is targeting it. It combines Google's visibility, Mandiant's frontline incident response expertise and VirusTotal's crowd-sourced detection into one verdict on indicators such as suspicious file hashes and domains. Security Command Center is the single place to discover misconfigurations and vulnerabilities across Google Cloud projects, rank which risks matter most and help fix them; continuous posture management there is what would have flagged a storage resource exposed to the internet for months. Google Security Operations is a unified platform for telemetry, threat intelligence, detection and response, replacing a pile of separate tools used by a security operations center. Gemini in Google Security Operations adds natural-language search, detection help and case summaries, which saves a small team hours of writing queries and reports.

concepts.heading: AI Protection and Model Armor
concepts.body: Companies that adopt generative AI create two separate security questions. The first is runtime: employees might paste customer data into prompts, or attackers might use prompt injection and jailbreaks to make an assistant misbehave. Model Armor answers this by screening prompts and responses for prompt injection, jailbreaks and sensitive data leaks. The second is visibility: several teams experiment in different projects and leadership does not know which models and AI assets exist or how risky they are. AI Protection in Security Command Center answers this by helping find AI assets and manage their threats and risks. An easy memory aid is that Model Armor looks at the content of each conversation as it happens, while AI Protection looks at the AI estate across the organization. Both belong to a layered approach where infrastructure, data, models and agents are each protected, and neither replaces access control through IAM.

concepts.heading: Protecting Networks, Access, Certificates, and Data
concepts.body: Several focused offerings round out the picture, and each matches one clear need. Cloud Armor provides DDoS protection and a web application firewall in front of load-balanced applications, so it fits a ticket seller expecting bots and traffic floods. Identity-Aware Proxy verifies identity and applies access policy per application request, letting employees and contractors reach internal web apps from anywhere without a traditional VPN, in line with zero trust. Certificate Manager automates getting, deploying and renewing TLS certificates, so public endpoints do not show browser warnings because someone forgot a renewal. Sensitive Data Protection discovers, classifies and de-identifies personal information across documents and tables. Confidential Computing keeps data encrypted while it is processed. For connectivity, Cloud Interconnect gives a dedicated high-bandwidth private link for a large site, and Cloud VPN gives quick encrypted connections over the internet for a small remote site.

concepts.heading: Trust, Compliance, Transparency, and Sovereignty
concepts.body: Customers also ask how they can trust the provider, and the exam links each question to a resource. For proof of independent verification, the Compliance resource center lets customers download audit reports and certifications, such as ISO/IEC 27001 and SOC reports, and see how controls map to standards; this is the answer for a bank whose regulator wants evidence. For questions about government requests for customer data, Google's Transparency Reports publicly share data about requests and the policies for responding. For control over where data is stored and processed and over who can access it, digital sovereignty and data residency choices, including sovereign cloud options with regional partners and customer-controlled key access, are the fit for a public-sector agency. Remember that compliance evidence helps the customer, but responsibility stays shared: the provider's certificates do not automatically certify the customer's own configuration.

examPoints: Security Command Center finds and ranks risks across projects, Google Threat Intelligence identifies who is targeting you, and Google Security Operations unifies detection and response; match the verb in the stem.
Model Armor screens each prompt and response at runtime, while AI Protection in Security Command Center gives visibility of AI assets and their risks across the organization.

Trust questions map to resources: Compliance resource center for audit reports, Transparency Reports for government requests, and sovereignty and residency choices for control over data location and access.

quiz.q: A software company is moving its internal tools to the cloud. The security team wants a user to reach each internal web application only after identity and context are checked, from home or an office, and without a company-wide VPN. Which Google Cloud offering fits?
choices: Cloud Armor, which filters traffic floods and web attacks in front of the applications at the network edge
Cloud VPN, which links the office network to Google Cloud over an encrypted internet connection
Identity-Aware Proxy, which checks identity and applies access policy for each request to an application
Certificate Manager, which automates the issue and renewal of certificates on public load balancers
quiz.explain: Identity-Aware Proxy provides identity-based, per-application access without a traditional VPN, which matches the zero trust idea. Cloud Armor defends against attacks and floods, Cloud VPN is a network link, and Certificate Manager handles certificates; none checks who the user is for each request.

quiz.q: A bank's audit committee asks for a single page showing which Google Cloud projects have exposed storage, risky settings or known vulnerabilities, ranked so the team fixes the worst first. Which product matches?
choices: Security Command Center, which finds, ranks and helps fix risks and misconfigurations across Google Cloud
Google Threat Intelligence, which gives a verdict on suspicious indicators using Mandiant and VirusTotal data
Model Armor, which screens prompts and responses of a company assistant for injection and data leaks
Cloud Interconnect, which provides a dedicated private connection between the bank's sites and Google Cloud
quiz.explain: Security Command Center is the place that discovers misconfigurations and vulnerabilities across projects and ranks the riskiest. Threat Intelligence tells you about attackers, Model Armor guards AI conversations, and Interconnect is a connectivity service.

days.recap: Google builds security into its layers (secure by design) and stacks controls (defense in depth). Match the product to the verb: Security Command Center finds risk, Threat Intelligence names attackers, Security Operations detects and responds, Model Armor screens prompts, AI Protection sees AI assets. Trust resources prove compliance.

days.title: Cost Management, Observability, and Reliability

concepts.heading: CapEx, OpEx, and Total Cost of Ownership
concepts.body: Two finance terms explain why the cloud changes budgets. Capital expenditure (CapEx) is up-front spending on assets, such as buying servers that are then depreciated over years. Operating expenditure (OpEx) is ongoing spending on running the business, such as paying each month for the resources you consume. Moving from owned data centers to Google Cloud shifts spend from CapEx to OpEx, because the company no longer buys and depreciates hardware up front. Total cost of ownership (TCO) is the idea that the true cost of an option includes everything needed to own and operate it, not only the purchase price. When a retailer compares its own servers with the cloud, the comparison should include staff time for patching, hardware replacement and routine maintenance, plus data center space, power and cooling. Counting only the price of the hardware makes on-premises look cheaper than it is. These are generally accepted finance definitions, applied to the cloud.

concepts.heading: FinOps and Cost Visibility
concepts.body: FinOps is the practice of bringing engineering, finance and business teams together so each shares accountability for cloud spend. It exists because cloud lets any engineer launch resources in minutes, while finance may see only one combined invoice at month end. The cure is transparency plus ownership: real-time cost visibility so each team owns the cost of what it runs. A useful frame sorts improvement into people, process and technology. People means skills and ownership, process means repeatable routines such as a monthly review where finance and engineering compare spend with forecasts and agree on follow-up actions, and technology means visibility and automation. On the technology side, Google Cloud's built-in tools, such as Cloud Billing reports and the FinOps hub, show cost and usage trends by service and project in one shared place, so team leads can see what they spend without waiting for the invoice.

concepts.heading: Resource Hierarchy, Budgets, Quotas, and Cheaper Capacity
concepts.body: The Google Cloud resource hierarchy runs from the organization through folders to projects and resources. Access control and policies set high in the hierarchy are inherited by everything below, so a bank can put its 40 retail projects in one folder, set the policy there and have any project created later inherit it. The organization level also gives auditors one view of all projects. For cost control, remember the difference between informing and limiting. A budget with alert thresholds, such as 50, 90 and 100 percent, only notifies recipients; by itself it does not stop resources. A quota restricts how much of a resource a project can use and blocks consumption beyond it, which protects a start-up from a coding mistake or stolen credentials creating thousands of machines overnight. To lower cost, Spot VMs give deep discounts for fault-tolerant, restartable work such as nightly rendering, and the Dynamic Workload Scheduler helps teams obtain scarce GPUs and TPUs when available without paying for idle reserved hardware.

concepts.heading: Observability: Monitoring, Logging, Trace, Profiler, and Error Reporting
concepts.body: Observability is the ability to understand what is happening inside a running system from the data it produces, and Google Cloud Observability groups the tools. Cloud Monitoring watches metrics, draws charts and sends alerts when, for example, response time passes a threshold. Cloud Logging keeps the searchable record of detailed events. When checkout is slow in an application made of several microservices and none reports errors, Cloud Trace follows a request across services and shows how much latency each step adds. When developers want to know which functions in production use the most CPU and memory, Cloud Profiler ties resource use to the code. When a release throws many exceptions, Error Reporting groups the error events by root cause and counts them so the team can triage. A good habit is to read the stem for the question being asked: where is the time spent, which code is expensive, which errors are most common, or tell me when a threshold is crossed.

concepts.heading: Reliability, SLI, SLO, SLA, and Resilience
concepts.body: Operational excellence means running workloads efficiently through automation, orchestration and data-driven insights, with continuous learning. Reliability is consistently doing the job correctly, while high availability is staying up through a component failure, often by running redundant copies in more than one zone or region. Data needs its own protection: replication keeps a copy in another location, which guards against a site failure but also copies mistakes, so backups that can be restored to an earlier state are still needed after an accidental deletion. The four golden signals, a generally accepted monitoring framework, are latency, traffic, errors and saturation; latency and errors are the most user-facing, and saturation warns that the service is nearing its limits before users notice. Three terms are measured, targeted and promised. A service level indicator (SLI) is the measured value, such as the percentage of successful requests. A service level objective (SLO) is the internal target for it, such as 99.95 percent. A service level agreement (SLA) is the contract promise to customers, with consequences such as credits.

examPoints: Moving from owned hardware to the cloud shifts spend from CapEx to OpEx, and TCO means counting all ownership costs, including staff time, space, power and cooling, not only the purchase price.
Budgets and reports inform, quotas limit; policies and access set high in the resource hierarchy are inherited by projects below.

Match observability tools to the question: Monitoring for metrics and alerts, Logging for event records, Trace for latency across services, Profiler for code resource use, Error Reporting for grouped errors; SLI measures, SLO targets and SLA promises.

quiz.q: A software company's head of finance notices that cloud spend keeps rising and no one team feels responsible. Engineers say that costs are finance's problem. Which approach best fits the FinOps idea?
choices: Share accountability among engineering, finance and business teams, supported by cost visibility that lets each team see what its own resources cost
Move all cloud purchases to finance, so that engineers must request approval before running any workload
Switch to a single large annual forecast, and review actual spend only once a year against it
Ask engineers to stop using managed services, because finance cannot see the details of what they cost
quiz.explain: FinOps makes engineering, finance and business jointly accountable for cloud cost and relies on transparency so teams own the cost of what they run. Central approval slows teams down, an annual review is too slow, and avoiding managed services does not create shared accountability.

quiz.q: A subscription video service promises customers 99.9 percent monthly availability and refunds a month's fee if it falls below. Its engineers measure the share of successful requests every minute and aim internally for 99.95 percent. Which statement correctly labels these items?
choices: The refund promise is the SLO, the internal aim is the SLA, and the measurement is the quota
The measurement is the SLA, the refund promise is the SLI, and the internal aim is the budget
The internal aim is the SLI, the measurement is the SLA, and the refund promise is the quota
The measurement is the SLI, the internal aim is the SLO, and the customer promise with the refund is the SLA
quiz.explain: The SLI is the measured value, the SLO is the target the engineers set, and the SLA is the contractual promise with consequences for the customer. The other labelings mix up which item is measured, which is targeted, and which is promised; quotas and budgets are cost and capacity controls, not reliability terms.

days.recap: The cloud moves spend from CapEx to OpEx, TCO counts every ownership cost, and FinOps shares cost accountability. Budgets alert while quotas limit; the hierarchy passes policy down. Pick the observability tool by question, and keep SLI measured, SLO targeted, SLA promised.

days.title: Final Review: Exam Format, Commonly Confused Pairs, and Test-Day Plan

concepts.heading: Know the Exam Format
concepts.body: The Cloud Digital Leader exam gives you 90 minutes for 50 to 60 multiple choice and multiple select questions. Google does not publish a pass mark, and the result is simply pass or fail. The exam is business level: it describes a business goal and asks which approach, product or benefit fits, and it does not ask for code, commands or console steps. It has six sections: digital transformation with Google Cloud, data transformation, AI, modernizing infrastructure and applications, and trust and security each carry about 18 percent, and scaling with operations carries about 10 percent. The weighting is nearly even, so no single area can carry you; plan time across all of them and give extra study to your weakest. The exam page says the new version of the exam went live in August 2026, so use current names such as Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Managed Service for Apache Spark, Cloud Run functions, Google Security Operations and Google Threat Intelligence.

concepts.heading: Confused Pairs: Digital Transformation and Data
concepts.body: Many wrong answers are real ideas attached to the wrong scenario. Hybrid cloud mixes private or on-premises with public cloud, while multicloud uses more than one public cloud provider. Latency is delay and bandwidth is capacity. A region holds several zones; multiple zones protect against a zone failure and multiple regions against a regional failure. In IaaS you control the operating system, in PaaS you write code on a platform the provider runs, and in SaaS you simply use the software. A database runs an application, a data warehouse combines data for analysis and reporting, and a data lake keeps raw data of every type. First-party data is your own, second-party is a partner's shared directly, and third-party is bought. Governance sets the rules, and open standards reduce lock-in. For storage, Spanner is global and strongly consistent, Cloud SQL is a familiar relational engine, AlloyDB is PostgreSQL-compatible for demanding workloads, Bigtable fits key-based time-series data, Firestore fits mobile documents, and BigQuery fits large-scale SQL analytics. On the processing chain, Pub/Sub ingests, Dataflow processes, BigQuery analyzes and Looker presents.

concepts.heading: Confused Pairs: AI and Modernization
concepts.body: In AI, business intelligence reports on historical data, machine learning predicts, and generative AI creates new content, while agentic AI plans and acts toward a goal through tools. Completeness, uniqueness, timeliness, validity, accuracy and consistency are different data-quality dimensions; a value can be valid and still wrong. For AI solutions, pre-trained APIs suit common tasks on a deadline, AutoML on Agent Platform suits labelled data with no ML coders, BigQuery ML suits SQL analysts, and custom training suits a unique objective. For migration, retire removes a workload, retain keeps it, rehost moves it as is, replatform adds targeted improvements, refactor changes the code, and reimagine rethinks the process. Compute Engine gives virtual machines with operating system control, GKE orchestrates many containers, Cloud Run runs stateless containers with minimal operations, and Cloud Run functions react to events. BigQuery Omni analyzes data in other clouds, AlloyDB Omni runs the database anywhere, and GKE Enterprise manages Kubernetes across environments. Apigee manages and monetizes APIs for an organization.

concepts.heading: Confused Pairs: Security and Operations
concepts.body: In security, authentication proves who you are, authorization decides what you may do and auditing records what happened. Data can be protected at rest, in transit and in use, and Confidential Computing is the in-use answer. Control is your decisions; compliance is meeting external rules. Security Command Center finds and ranks risks, Google Threat Intelligence names who is targeting you, Google Security Operations unifies detection and response, Model Armor screens prompts and responses, and AI Protection gives visibility of AI assets. Cloud Armor defends against DDoS and web attacks, Identity-Aware Proxy gives per-application access without a VPN, and Sensitive Data Protection finds and de-identifies sensitive data. For operations, CapEx is up-front asset spending and OpEx is ongoing running cost. A budget alerts but a quota limits. Replication protects against a site failure but copies mistakes, so backups are also needed. Cloud Monitoring alerts on metrics, Cloud Logging keeps event records, Cloud Trace finds slow steps across services, and SLI, SLO and SLA are measured, targeted and promised.

concepts.heading: Test-Day Plan and Error Log
concepts.body: Keep an error log. For every practice question you miss or guess, write the pair of ideas you confused, such as hybrid versus multicloud, replatform versus refactor, budget versus quota or Model Armor versus AI Protection, and the clue in the stem that should have decided it. Reviewing pairs is faster than rereading everything. On test day, check your room, webcam and system, or arrive early, and read the exam instructions. Read each scenario for the deciding phrase before looking at the choices, such as no data science team, existing Spark jobs, organization-wide view, or must stay encrypted while processed. Then eliminate choices that solve a different problem. Multiple select stems say how many to pick, so count them. Answer what you know first, mark uncertain items for review where allowed, and watch the 90-minute timer. Because the pass mark is not published, aim to answer every question and leave none blank. Check Google's certification page for current retake rules before booking another attempt.

examPoints: Six sections of roughly equal weight (about 18 percent each, with scaling with operations at about 10 percent) mean breadth beats depth: no area can be skipped.

A stem that lists look-alike products is testing the purpose of each, so find the deciding phrase, such as existing Spark jobs, global strong consistency, per-application access, or organization-wide visibility.

A stem that offers a tool that only informs versus one that enforces is testing the pair: budgets alert and quotas limit, replication copies and backups restore, authentication proves and authorization permits.

quiz.q: A learner mixes up two cost and capacity controls. Which statement correctly separates a budget from a quota?
choices: A budget blocks all use of a resource at the limit, while a quota only emails an alert as spending grows
A budget and a quota both stop resources when exceeded, but only a quota can be set on a folder
A budget notifies people as spend crosses thresholds, while a quota restricts how much of a resource a project can use
A budget measures service availability for customers, while a quota sets the contract credits for downtime
quiz.explain: Budget thresholds are alerts only, so someone must act, whereas a quota is a limit that blocks use beyond it. The first choice swaps the two, and the others invent behaviors: availability targets are SLOs and contract credits belong to an SLA.

quiz.q: A company's data team already runs hundreds of Spark and Hadoop jobs on its own cluster. It wants to move them to Google Cloud quickly with few code changes and less cluster upkeep. Which choice fits best?
choices: Rebuild every job from scratch as a new Dataflow pipeline before moving anything, to get the cleanest design
Move the jobs to Managed Service for Apache Spark, which runs existing Spark and Hadoop workloads as a managed service
Load the raw files into Firestore, so that the jobs can read documents instead of files in a cluster
Replace the jobs with Looker dashboards, because dashboards remove the need for any data processing
quiz.explain: Existing Spark and Hadoop workloads move naturally to Managed Service for Apache Spark, while Dataflow suits new managed pipelines and would need a rebuild. Firestore is a document database for apps, and Looker presents results rather than running the processing.

days.recap: The exam is 90 minutes with 50 to 60 questions, no published pass mark, and six sections of near-equal weight. Drill the confused pairs across all of them, keep an error log with the deciding clue, answer every question, and check Google's current retake rules before booking again.
